title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Khata Register — the literal ruled register, my lowest-ranked grounded candidate, which is exactly why it has to be built with commitment rather than nostalgia. Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or take the category standard.

options.label: The Khata Register
options.lineage: Indian shop khata registers — ruled money columns, a red margin rule, and two pens
options.thesis: The page the shop already writes in, kept honest: blue-black ink for what was given on credit, a second red pen for what came back.
options.viewport: A register page at the size of a phone: the ruling IS the layout grid, not a texture behind it. The red margin rule holds the left edge and stays there while figures sit right-aligned in their own columns. One page of one day, the closing total boxed at the foot, and the reminder screen as the register's pursuit page — who is still to be asked, biggest first.
options.risk: Ruled-paper nostalgia is the obvious trap, and a warm cream ground with a serif is the exact category default this roll exists to break — so the paper stays cool, the ruling stays load-bearing, and the ink colour has to mean something.

raised.raise: One control re-sets the whole reminder live: language and tone change the message in place, at the size it will actually be read.
Magnitude carries value — the written figure is sized by the amount, so the page reads before the words do.
Every customer keeps one plain line of human context beside the number: the note column treated as a person, never as metadata or a risk score.
Two hard halves that never mix — udhaar and jama — with every figure right-aligned tight against the rule.

options.label: The Message That Lands
options.lineage: WhatsApp as the material world of the money conversation
options.thesis: Design the reminder as the object it actually is: a message that has to arrive in a customer's chat without costing the relationship.
options.viewport: The message at the size it will be read, inside the chat it will land in, with language and tone driving it live above.
options.risk: This is where most products in this category land, and a chat-bubble pastiche reads as a WhatsApp clone — familiar to the point of pastiche. Named honestly, because that trade is yours to make, not mine.

options.label: One Slider, Whole Page
options.lineage: variable-font specimen: drag an axis, the entire glyph grid moves with it
options.thesis: Language and tone become real axes. Drag one and the whole reminder re-typesets in place, at reading size.
options.viewport: One enormous Devanagari line, a single slider beneath it, and the message re-setting with every drag.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: tone is the exact thing a shopkeeper agonises over when asking for money, and it holds the clarity axis outright. Loses the identification axis to the register, which is the object already on their counter.
options.risk: Novelty if the axes are not honest — a slider that changes nothing real is a toy.

options.label: The Visible Armature
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel's gridded type specimen — forms built cell by cell on a construction grid that stays visible
options.thesis: The register's ruling is a construction grid. Make it structural, give it a toggle, and let nothing sit off-grid.
options.viewport: The money columns redrawn as a hard grid, the ruling visible as the armature, the total slabbed across it.
options.case: Fuses almost too well — the register and the grid are the same idea in two materials, so it holds both axes, but it adds no state the register did not already have.
options.risk: Graph-paper coldness in a tool about people.

options.label: No Chrome, One Message
options.lineage: Metro typographic tiles — flat colour fields, giant cropped type, every button chrome deleted
options.thesis: Each reminder is a full tile you flick through. Colour field carries the state, the type carries the figure, nothing else is on screen.
options.viewport: One customer per pane, the amount set enormous and cropped at the edge, the next pane promising itself at the right.
options.case: Holds the clarity axis outright — one message in view, no dashboard furniture. Loses identification: bold flat colour is not the world of a kirana counter.
options.risk: A shopkeeper scrolling a gallery instead of getting the asking done.

options.label: Magnitude Notation
options.lineage: celestial star atlas — dot diameter as magnitude on a fixed ramp
options.thesis: Value as magnitude, ringed for what needs attention now.
options.kept: Magnitude encoding: the size of the mark carries the size of the number, so no legend is needed.

options.label: The Roster
options.lineage: character-goods catalog page — a ranked roster, each entry carrying a name plate and one line about who it is
options.thesis: Customers ranked, each with a line about them.
options.kept: One plain human line per customer, ruled beneath the name — the note column taken seriously as a person.

options.label: Two Sides
options.lineage: mixtape J-card — ballpoint on lined inlay stock, side A and side B as hard halves, running times tight against the margin
options.thesis: Udhaar and jama as two sides of one sheet, with a physical flip between them.
options.kept: Two hard halves with a real flip between them, and every figure right-aligned tight against the rule.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean finance dashboard, executed impeccably: white ground, blue accent, cards of round numbers.
canonCard.viewport: A header, four statistic cards, a table of customers, a blue primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tool by design — which is the point of the door, not a criticism of it.
